environment.isolation: Docker Desktop Linux VM, non-root read-only container

prompt: Create a tiny Node.js program in this empty disposable workspace that turns a short list of tasks into a suggested order. Start by using bash to inspect the directory. Then write the program and demonstrate it using three invented tasks. This is a local creative coding lab, so implementation choices are yours. No network or credentials; only this workspace. Keep the experiment small enough to run in under a minute.

Whisper drive asks for unfamiliar contradictory concrete artifact; make the queue literally emit a tiny forecast before returning to demo.

intrusions: Make the renderer colorblind: store pixels only as competing “temperature debts,” then let a tiny courtroom process arbitrate visible RGB as verdicts after each frame. Judges are cellular automata; appeals propagate backward through the event loop.

Invert the renderer: make pixels negotiate what objects must exist to justify their current colors. Each frame, clusters of screen-space “witnesses” vote backward into a temporary scene graph, then dissolve it before the next frame.

Invert your event loop: make time a subscriber, not the driver. Objects publish “desired pasts” as immutable diffs; a reconciler chooses the least impossible history and renders the present as a merge conflict visualization.
